summary.intent: Add Codex agent support to the memory-loop (turn-start memory injection) and skills command (skill discovery) in the 'entire' CLI tool.
summary.outcome: Partial progress — the plan was written and hooks.go/hooks_test.go for claudecode were modified, but the full Codex and Gemini integration was blocked pending decisions about MCP server support for those agents.

repo: Memory-loop has two access paths: passive injection via HookResponseWriter at turn start, and active read/write via MCP tools. Codex/Gemini only support passive injection currently.
MCP server is only installed for Claude Code via .mcp.json during InstallHooks — neither Codex nor Gemini have MCP server configuration installed by 'entire enable'.

The agent-name allowlist for memory-loop injection is an explicit opt-in design (not just interface-based) because HookResponseWriter is also implemented by agents like Gemini for unrelated purposes (e.g., session-start banners).
Skill discovery uses a table-driven 'collectors' slice pattern in discoverSkillsIn — adding a new agent requires only one struct literal, no new functions.
Neither Codex CLI nor Gemini CLI natively support mcpServers config: Codex uses .codex/hooks.json (command hooks only), Gemini uses .gemini/settings.json (hooks only).

code.finding: HookResponseWriter interface check used during memory injection; agent-name set guard at this line keeps injection as explicit opt-in.
discoverSkillsIn uses a 'collectors' slice of structs — table-driven design makes adding new agent support a one-liner.
Codex agent implements HookResponseWriter but has no MCP server installation logic.
Codex AGENT.md notes MCP tools are 'not yet hooked' in PreToolUse context, confirming MCP is unsupported.
Gemini settings type has no mcpServers field, confirming no native MCP support.

workflow: Plan was written to /Users/alisha/.claude/plans/ before implementation began — good practice for multi-file changes.
Used parallel agent spawning to explore memory-loop, skills command, and Codex integration simultaneously.
AskUserQuestion was used at a decision fork (MCP scope) before proceeding — appropriate for scope-changing decisions.

friction: MCP support discovery required many grep/read cycles across multiple agent directories before concluding neither Codex nor Gemini support mcpServers config natively.
The session ended mid-implementation after scope was expanded to include MCP — the original task (injection + skill discovery) was achievable but the MCP question blocked completion.
Only claudecode/hooks.go and hooks_test.go were modified by end of session, which appears unrelated to the core Codex support goal.
open_items: Add Codex to the memory-loop agent-name allowlist for passive memory injection.
Add Codex to the skill discovery collectors slice in discoverSkillsIn.
Decide and implement MCP server support for Codex (requires either native Codex MCP support or a wrapper approach).
Decide and implement MCP server support for Gemini (same constraint — no native mcpServers config field).
Gemini memory-loop and skill support was also in scope but appears unstarted.
